articleTitle: Power quality issues within modern industrial facilities
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: Two case studied performed by an electric utility are presented in which industrial facilities experienced operational problems due to power conversion equipment. The case studies describe two common problems associated with power conversion devices: line voltage notching and harmonic current amplification caused by parallel resonance. The problems associated with each case, their analyses, and the steps taken to resolve them are reported.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimizing system coordination and overcurrent protection with zone selective interlocking
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: After a review of the currently available types of low-voltage circuit breakers and fuses, a discussion is presented of how to optimize low-voltage distribution for selectively coordinated systems through the use of properly selected overcurrent protection devices. Topics covered include how these components respond during overcurrent conditions and how system coordination is enhanced by zone selective interlocking.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Brushless DC-a modern approach to variable speed drives
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: The theory of brushless DC motor operation is briefly outlined. Similarities and differences with other types of drives are discussed, and a justification given for the use of the term brushless DC, drive as a distinct type of drive as opposed to referring it to as simply a variant of the variable-frequency drive. A comparison is made of operating characteristics and parameters of the brushless DC and traditional DC drives in the small-to-medium-horsepower range (to 150 hp). Particular emphasis is placed on the advantages to the end-user of the drive and how these advantages affect production, service, and operating cost. Included is information on efficiency, power factor, motor heating, and breakaway torque. Application benefits are discussed demonstrating some of the advantages of using brushless DC drives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Disconnecting means: an examination of the National Code and review of current applications
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: The requirements of the 1990 National Electric Code (NEC) regarding disconnecting means are described with emphasis on location of disconnect switches, the requirements for fusing, sizing, and other considerations associated with the proper operation of disconnecting devices. Brief mention is made of the results of a survey of industry users indicating the degree to which these respondents comply with the NEC.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Temperature control of heated rolls using Honeywell series 9000 controllers
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: Current sensor technology and control strategies to optimize heated roll control are briefly reviewed as background for a description of the Honeywell Series 9000 controller, a small process control system that can control heated rolls. The Series 9000 controller combines the capabilities of an industrial programmable controller and the functionality of a process control system. Programming is accomplished in a Samma-type language. The process controller or loop control module handles 32 loops of proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control while combining the functionality of a programmable controller, chart recorders, and set point programmers, as well as providing an operator interface and supervisory functionality. All of the functions of the loop controller and operator interface functions are contained in the loop processor module. All configuration is done with a mouse through the configuration program which runs under Microsoft Windows.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: The basic operating principles of thyristors and silicon-controlled rectifiers (SCRs) are reviewed, and basic troubleshooting techniques for these devices used in solid-state motor controllers are outlined. The information covered is basic enough to also be applicable to SCRs in variable-frequency drives as well as solid-state reduced voltage starters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Disconnect switch standards and test procedures
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: UL (Underwriters Laboratories) and NEMA (National Electrical Manufacturers Association) design standards and NEC (National Electrical Code) installation practices are reviewed to provide a better understanding of safety switch product capabilities and applications. The test procedures applicable to switch products are discussed. Application requirements outside the parameters of these tests should be considered unusual applications and should be reviewed with the manufacturer. The standards as they relate to products listed as general duty and heavy duty are considered. Product life and service requirements are related to the choice of a heavy or general duty switch, depending on the nature of the application. The standards for enclosure test procedures relating to the various enclosure types are described. As defined, enclosures are intended to provide a degree of protection to the equipment within them, and an understanding of the construction requirements will aid in identifying the correct type for common application needs. Also included ar misapplication issues that are sometimes assumed by untrained personnel who utilize the general descriptions of these enclosure types without a thorough understanding of the applicable design standards.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: AC vector drive using current regulated PWM
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: A brief review of motor field AC theory is presented, and current-regulated pulse-width modulation (CRPWM) is compared to current source inversion (CSI-type) vector control. The advantages of CRPWM are discussed. The flexibility in using AC vector control drives compared to DC is stressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application considerations of adjustable frequency extruder drives
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: The strengths and the limitations of various AC motor drive designs as they relate to several extrusion applications are examined. AC drives using variable voltage control, current source inversion, pulse-width modulation, vector control, and brushless AC or DC motors are considered. AC-drive strength and weaknesses are discussed. Digital control of the drives and their communications interfaces are noted, and factors influencing the proper selection of an AC drive for extruder use are enumerated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: IEC and NEMA motor starters: understanding the differences
publicationTitle: Annual IEEE Conference on Textile, Fiber and Film Industry
abstract: After a historical review of the IEC (International Electrotechnical Commission), NEMA (National Electrical Manufacturers' Association), and UL (Underwriters Laboratories) and their goals, a description is given of how differences in market forces and conditions in Europe caused IEC-type contactors to develop differently from NEMA-type contactors. These dissimilarities also caused IEC-type overloads to evolve differently. Since the introduction of IEC-type overload relays in the North American market has caused problems for U S engineers, a detailed review of operational and feature differences of IEC- and NEMA-type specified devices is given. Eight issues that should be considered when making a choice between IEC-type and NEMA-type starters are discussed: starter size; starter price; contactor performance; contactor application; overload relay trip characteristics; overload relay reset mechanism characteristics; and fault-withstand capability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
